readings.title: The Provocation of Ishbosheth
readings.subtitle: A reckless accusation concerning a concubine fractures the adversarial stronghold.
readings.text: [6] And it came to be, while there was fighting between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Daviḏ, that Aḇnĕr was strengthening himself in the house of Sha’ul. [7] And Sha’ul had a concubine, whose name was Ritspah, daughter of Ayah. And Ishbosheth said to Aḇnĕr, “Why have you gone in to <dn>את</dn> my father’s concubine?”

readings.title: Abner’s Oath of Transfer
readings.subtitle: Abner recognizes YeHoVaH's decree and swears to establish the throne of Daviḏ.
readings.text: [8] And Aḇnĕr was very displeased at the words of Ishbosheth, and said, “Am <dn>I</dn> a dog’s head that belongs to Yehuḏah, that <dn>I</dn> show loving-commitment to the house of Sha’ul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends today, and have not let you fall into the hand of Daviḏ, that you charge me today with a sin concerning this woman? [9] “<dn>Elohim</dn> does so to Aḇnĕr, and more also, if <dn>I</dn> do not do for Daviḏ as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn to <dn>him</dn>: [10] to cause <dn>את</dn> the reign to pass over from the house of Sha’ul, and to raise up <dn>את</dn> the throne of Daviḏ over Yisra’ĕl and over Yehuḏah, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa.” [11] And he was unable to answer Aḇnĕr another word, because he feared him.

readings.title: The Covenant of Return
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ demands the restoration of his legal wife, Miḵal, before entertaining any alliance.
readings.text: [12] And Aḇnĕr sent messengers on his behalf to Daviḏ, saying, “Whose is the land?” saying also, “Make your covenant with me, and see, my hand is with you to bring all Yisra’ĕl to you.” [13] And Daviḏ said, “Good, <dn>I</dn> make a covenant with you. Only one matter <dn>I</dn> am asking of you: you do not see <dn>את</dn> my face unless you first bring <dn>את</dn> Miḵal, daughter of Sha’ul, when you come to see my face.”

readings.title: Severing the Unlawful Tie
readings.subtitle: Miḵal is extracted from Palti’ĕl, enforcing righteous bounds over emotional attachments.
readings.text: [14] Daviḏ then sent messengers to Ishbosheth son of Sha’ul, saying, “Give me <dn>את</dn> my wife Miḵal, to whom <dn>I</dn> became engaged for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.” [15] And Ishbosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Palti’ĕl son of Layish. [16] But her husband went with her to Baḥurim, going on and weeping behind her. And Aḇnĕr said to him, “Go, turn back!” And he turned back.

readings.title: Reminding Israel of the Prophetic Decree
readings.subtitle: Abner calls the elders to execute YeHoVaH's promised deliverance through Daviḏ.
readings.text: [17] And Aḇnĕr had a word with the elders of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “In time past you were seeking for Daviḏ to be sovereign over you. [18] “And now, do it! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken of Daviḏ, saying, <dq>‘By the hand of <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, <dn>I</dn> save <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl from the hand of the Philistines and the hand of all their enemies.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Feast of Peace
readings.subtitle: A temporary harmony is established as Abner departs to rally the entire nation.
readings.text: [19] And Aḇnĕr also spoke in the hearing of Binyamin. And Aḇnĕr also went to speak in the hearing of Daviḏ in Ḥeḇron all that seemed good to Yisra’ĕl and all the house of Binyamin. [20] And Aḇnĕr and twenty men with him came to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron. And Daviḏ made a feast for Aḇnĕr and the men who were with him. [21] And Aḇnĕr said to Daviḏ, “Let me arise and go, and gather all Yisra’ĕl to my master the sovereign, and let them make a covenant with you, and you shall reign over all that your being desires.” And Daviḏ sent Aḇnĕr away, and he went in peace.

readings.title: The Accuser Returns
readings.subtitle: Operating in retributive justice, Yo’aḇ questions the sovereign's wisdom and assumes treason.
readings.text: [22] And see, the servants of Daviḏ and Yo’aḇ came from a raid and brought much spoil with them. But Aḇnĕr was not with Daviḏ in Ḥeḇron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace. [23] And Yo’aḇ and all the army that was with him came, and they reported to Yo’aḇ, saying, “Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to the sovereign, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace.” [24] And Yo’aḇ went to the sovereign and said, “What have you done? See, Aḇnĕr has come to you! Why is it that you sent him away, and he has already gone? [25] “You know that Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to deceive you, to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing.”

readings.title: Blood in the Gate
readings.subtitle: Yo’aḇ circumvents the righteous court to extract zero-sum revenge for his brother's blood.
readings.text: [26] Yo’aḇ then left Daviḏ, and he sent messengers after Aḇnĕr, who brought him back from the well of Sirah. But Daviḏ did not know it. [27] Thus Aḇnĕr returned to Ḥeḇron, and Yo’aḇ took him aside in the gate to speak with him privately, and there struck him in the stomach, so that he died for the blood of Asah’ĕl his brother.

readings.title: The Curse of Unrighteous Atonement
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ publicly washes his hands of the systemic friction and pronounces a generational curse on Yo’aḇ's house.
readings.text: [28] And when Daviḏ heard it afterwards, he said, “<dn>My</dn> reign and <dn>I</dn> are guiltless before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forever of the blood of Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr. [29] “Let it rest on the head of Yo’aḇ and on all his father’s house. And let there never fail to be in the house of Yo’aḇ one who has a discharge or is a leper, or who is taking hold of a staff or falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.” [30] So Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother killed <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr, because he had killed their brother Asah’ĕl at Giḇ’on in the battle.

readings.title: The Sovereign's Lament
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ commands public repentance and leads the mourning for a fallen prince in Israel.
readings.text: [31] And Daviḏ said to Yo’aḇ and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your garments, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn for Aḇnĕr.” And Sovereign Daviḏ followed the coffin. [32] And they buried Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron. And the sovereign lifted up his voice and wept at the burial-site of Aḇnĕr, and all the people wept. [33] And the sovereign sang a lament over Aḇnĕr and said, “Should Aḇnĕr die as a fool dies? [34] “Your hands were not bound nor your feet put into shackles. As one falls before sons of evil, so you fell.” And all the people wept over him again.

readings.title: Fasting for National Trust
readings.subtitle: By demonstrating absolute empathy, Daviḏ proves his innocence and exposes the harshness of retributive operators.
readings.text: [35] And all the people came to cause Daviḏ to eat food while it was still day, but Daviḏ swore, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> do so to me, and more also, if <dn>I</dn> taste bread or whatever else till the sun goes down!” [36] And all the people took note of it, and it was good in their eyes, since whatever the sovereign did was good in the eyes of all the people. [37] And all the people and all Yisra’ĕl knew that day that it had not been the sovereign’s intent to kill Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr. [38] The sovereign also said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great one has fallen in Yisra’ĕl today? [39] “And <dn>I</dn> am weak today, though anointed sovereign. And these men, the sons of Tseruyah, are too harsh for me. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> repay the evil-doer according to his evil.”

readings.title: The Loss of Heart
readings.subtitle: With their primary military strength severed, the illegitimate administration of Ishbosheth faces structural failure.
readings.text: [1] And the son of Sha’ul heard that Aḇnĕr had died in Ḥeḇron, and he lost heart, and all Yisra’ĕl was troubled. [2] And the son of Sha’ul had two men, commanders of bands, and the name of one was Ba’anah and the name of the other Rĕḵaḇ, sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, of the children of Binyamin. For Be’ĕroth was also reckoned to Binyamin, [3] because the Be’ĕrothites fled to Gittayim and have been sojourners there until this day.

readings.title: The Strike at Noon
readings.subtitle: Two captains execute a treacherous assassination, falsely attributing their violent opportunism to YeHoVaH's will.
readings.text: [5] So the sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, Rĕḵaḇ and Ba’anah, went and came at about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who was lying on his bed at noon. [6] And they came into the midst of the house, to fetch wheat, and they struck him in the stomach, and Rĕḵaḇ and Ba’anah his brother escaped. [7] Thus they came into the house when he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him, and slew him, and beheaded <dn>את</dn> him. And they took <dn>את</dn> his head, and went the way of the desert plain all night, [8] and brought <dn>את</dn> the head of Ishbosheth to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron, and said to the sovereign, “See, the head of Ishbosheth, the son of Sha’ul your enemy, who sought your life. So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>my</dn> master the sovereign vengeance on Sha’ul and his seed this day.”

readings.title: The Wages of Unrighteousness
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ entirely rejects the adversary's method of advancement, dealing absolute justice to the perpetrators.
readings.text: [9] And Daviḏ answered Rĕḵaḇ and Ba’anah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, and said to them, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, who has ransomed <dn>my</dn> life out of all distress, [10] when someone reported to me, saying, ‘See, Sha’ul is dead,’ and he was a bearer of good news in his own eyes, <dn>I</dn> then took hold of him and killed him in Tsiqlaḡ, which was the reward <dn>I</dn> gave him for his news. [11] “How much more, when wrong men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed, should <dn>I</dn> not now require <dn>את</dn> his blood at your hand and remove <dn>את</dn> you from the earth?” [12] And Daviḏ commanded his young men, and they killed them, and cut off <dn>את</dn> their hands and <dn>את</dn> their feet, and hanged them by the pool in Ḥeḇron. And they took <dn>את</dn> the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the burial-site of Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron.
